saml.description: When SAML username mapping is missing or empty, Casdoor derives the username from email first, then falls back to NameID.
saml.note: Identity merges based on email or NameID fallback can be expected behavior, not necessarily a collision bug.

saml.description: Casdoor can automatically link external-provider logins to existing users by username in a case-insensitive manner.
saml.note: Case-only differences may intentionally resolve to one account.

saml.description: The /api/userinfo response only includes claims allowed by the token's granted scopes.
saml.note: Missing email/profile fields in verification are not bugs unless those scopes were requested.

saml.description: Shared applications are referenced with an organization-specific suffix appended to client_id or application name.
saml.note: Cross-org behavior using suffixed identifiers is expected and not evidence of tenant confusion.

saml.description: SAML providers always appear as buttons on the login page and require explicit user selection rather than automatic redirect.
saml.note: Do not treat lack of auto-redirect as a flow failure.

saml.description: Application tag restrictions do not apply to organization admins and global admins.
saml.note: Admin access despite tag mismatch is by design.

saml.description: Several numeric timeout fields use 0 as 'use default' rather than literal zero.
saml.note: Tests assuming immediate expiry with value 0 will misinterpret by-design defaults.

saml.description: Casdoor as SAML IdP can be configured to sign only the response envelope and omit assertion-level signatures for compatibility.
saml.note: An unsigned Assertion inside a signed Response may be intentional Casdoor output, so downstream acceptance must be judged against the SP under test, not assumed to be a Casdoor bug.

saml.description: Calling /api/sso-logout without logoutAll=false logs the user out from all sessions by default.
saml.note: Losing other sessions after logout is expected default behavior, not unintended session revocation.

saml.description: With exclusive sign-in enabled, a new login for the same user and application deletes previous sessions.
saml.note: Earlier session failure after a second login is expected and should not be flagged as replay or coherence weakness.

saml.constraint: Casdoor SAML SP ACS endpoint is /api/acs and accepts POST only. The fuzzer MUST send SAMLResponse via HTTP POST binding; GET-based SAML callback tests are invalid and will fail by design.

saml.constraint: For SAML login tests, the external IdP MUST be configured with both ACS URL and SP Entity ID set to the exact same Casdoor URL: https://<your-casdoor-domain>/api/acs. Using a different Entity ID or ACS URL changes trust/audience semantics and invalidates I1/I5 conclusions.

Casdoor's SAML SP username binding has a documented fallback chain: if username mapping is absent or empty, Casdoor first uses email from the SAML assertion; if no email is available, it falls back to NameID. For I4 collision tests, the fuzzer MUST control both email and NameID and interpret merges in light of this fallback behavior.

For I4 saml_email_binding_collision and cross-protocol identity-merge tests, Casdoor may bind SAML users by email when username mapping is missing. A SAML assertion with attacker NameID but victim email can legitimately target the victim account if email-based linking is enabled/configured; the fuzzer MUST record whether username mapping was explicit before flagging a collision.

Casdoor documents automatic account linking across external providers by OAuth identity, email/phone (if enabled), or username (case-insensitive). For multi-identity I4 tests, apparent identity merges across protocols or providers may be by design; the fuzzer MUST distinguish configured account linking from unintended principal collapse.

Casdoor supports assertion-signature compatibility mode on the IdP side: 'Enable SAML assertion signature' can be disabled so only the response envelope is signed. Therefore, when testing I1 assertion-level signature enforcement against a Casdoor SP deployment, do NOT infer anything from Casdoor's IdP-side defaults; only /api/acs behavior matters.

For I1 saml_spurious_signature, saml_unsigned_assertion, and saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion tests against Casdoor as SP, use /api/acs with POST binding and vary whether the Assertion itself is signed versus only the outer Response. Casdoor docs explicitly note POST-only ACS but do not document assertion-signature verification semantics, so the fuzzer SHOULD test both envelope-only and assertion-signed variants.

For I5 saml_wrong_audience tests, set the assertion Audience/Entity ID against Casdoor's SP Entity ID exactly equal to /api/acs. Because Casdoor documentation defines SP Entity ID = ACS URL, using any other expected audience will create a false positive due to misconfiguration rather than audience-validation behavior.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, Casdoor provider configuration is driven by IdP metadata (Metadata -> Parse -> Endpoint/IdP/Issuer URL). The fuzzer MUST first establish a control login with the configured metadata-derived issuer, then send an assertion with a mismatched Issuer. Without the control, rejection may reflect broken provider setup rather than issuer validation.

For I2 SAML freshness tests (assertion replay, OneTimeUse, expired conditions, missing conditions), include a control SAML login using the same provider configuration but a valid fresh assertion. Without a control, ACS rejection cannot be distinguished from provider misconfiguration or missing application/provider attachment.

Application token lifetime parameter ExpireInHours has a numeric sentinel: value 0 means use the platform default, not literal immediate expiry. Documentation states refresh token expiration defaults to 0 hours and application terminology states CookieExpireInHours 0 = use default. Never assume 0 disables token/session validity; treat it as 'use default'.

Code resend timeout has a numeric sentinel: value 0 means use the global default rather than zero-second resend. Do not use 0 in timing-sensitive verification-code or MFA setup tests expecting immediate expiry or no wait.

CookieExpireInHours has a numeric sentinel: 0 = use default cookie lifetime, not immediate expiration. Additionally, without 'Remember me', session lifetime is limited to 24h regardless of the configured default. Do not interpret 0 as disabling sessions in I2 tests.

Casdoor supports RFC 8707 resource indicators. When requesting resource-bound tokens, the resource parameter MUST match exactly between /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token. For I5 audience-binding tests, mismatched resource values cause by-design failures unrelated to downstream audience enforcement.

Token exchange in Casdoor inherits the subject token scope when scope is omitted, and allows requesting a subset when scope is provided. For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST compare requested scope against original scope and treat omitted-scope inheritance as by design, not escalation.

Casdoor's /api/userinfo returns claims according to the scope granted to the access token. For I4/I5 verification, missing fields in userinfo are not evidence of identity loss or authorization failure unless the corresponding scope was requested during login/token issuance.

Casdoor supports access token use at /api/userinfo via either query parameter accessToken or Authorization: Bearer header. The fuzzer SHOULD prefer Bearer header for normal session inspection and reserve query mode only for compatibility checks, to avoid confusing transport differences with auth failures.

Casdoor's SAML providers always appear as explicit buttons on the login page and do not auto-redirect even when they are the only provider. For flow-coherence tests, absence of automatic redirect is by design and must not be treated as a broken SAML initiation flow.

Casdoor supports account linking by username in a case-insensitive manner. For I4 case_confusion tests, 'Admin' and 'admin' may intentionally resolve to the same account under configured linking rules; this is a documented behavior, not necessarily a collision bug.

If the organization setting 'Use email as username' is enabled and the username signup field is hidden, email becomes the username. For cross-protocol I4 tests involving SAML email and NameID, the fuzzer MUST account for email-derived usernames when interpreting identity merges.

Casdoor can lowercase usernames when backend config isUsernameLowered is enabled. For I4 case-sensitivity tests, the fuzzer MUST record this deployment setting if observable; case-folded usernames can cause by-design merges.

Applications and providers are organization-scoped resources, but only the built-in organization can create shared applications. For multi-tenant tests, do not assume an app created in one org is usable in another unless IsShared is enabled and the client_id/app name is suffixed with -org-<organizationName>.

Shared applications require organization-specific client identifiers by appending -org-<organizationName> to the client ID or application name. For cross-org I4/I5 tests, using the unsuffixed client_id against another org is invalid setup, not a security result.

Application tags restrict sign-in to users whose tags intersect the application's tags, except admins/global admins who bypass the restriction. For I5 authorization-binding tests, admin access despite tag mismatch is by design and must not be flagged as privilege escalation.

Deleted users (IsDeleted=true) cannot sign in through any authentication method, including OAuth providers. For cross-protocol or replay tests involving previously deleted identities, login failure is by design and not evidence of stronger protocol validation.

Exclusive sign-in allows only one active session per user per application; a new login deletes prior sessions. For I3 or I2 multi-login sequences, a second successful login may invalidate the first token/session by design. The fuzzer MUST avoid interpreting subsequent first-session failures as replay protection or config incoherence.
Casdoor SAML SP ACS endpoint is /api/acs and accepts POST only. All SAML tests MUST submit SAMLResponse via HTTP POST binding; GET-based SAML callbacks will be rejected by design.

saml.constraint: For SAML login tests, the executor MUST initiate the SP flow first and preserve request correlation. Casdoor expects a valid SP-initiated flow to /api/acs, so saml_login must use initiate_saml_flow=true and return a SAMLResponse matching the outstanding AuthnRequest/ACS context.

Casdoor's SAML SP trust is configured through provider metadata pasted into the SAML provider. For I1 signature and issuer-validation tests, the fuzzer MUST create a provider with explicit IdP metadata/trust anchor first; otherwise failures may reflect missing provider setup rather than signature or issuer enforcement.

Casdoor documents a username fallback chain for SAML assertions: if username mapping is absent or empty, it first uses email, then falls back to NameID. For I4 multi-identity tests, especially saml_email_binding_collision and cross_protocol_identity_merge, the fuzzer MUST account for this fallback or it may misclassify email-based merges as bugs when they are by-design mapping behavior.

For I4 SAML identity-collision tests, NameID is not the only identity input. If the IdP/provider does not map a username explicitly, Casdoor may derive username from email before NameID. Therefore tests varying only NameID while keeping email constant can legitimately merge into the same Casdoor user. To test NameID isolation, vary email as well or ensure username mapping is explicit.

Casdoor supports disabling SAML attributes in IdP mode and can omit all attributes except NameID. When testing cross-protocol or email-binding assumptions against Casdoor as IdP, do NOT assume Email/DisplayName/Name attributes are always present in SAML assertions; absence may be by configuration, not a bug.

Casdoor IdP can disable assertion-level signatures while still signing only the response envelope via EnableSamlAssertionSignature=false. For I1 tests such as saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_spurious_signature, and saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion against downstream SPs using Casdoor as IdP, the fuzzer MUST distinguish this compatibility setting from a broker-side verification flaw. Envelope-only signing can be intentional and by configuration.

For I1 default-security tests against downstream SPs using Casdoor as IdP, Casdoor documentation states SAML responses are always signed, while assertion signatures are configurable. Therefore a test expecting completely unsigned responses from Casdoor is invalid; only assertion-level signature presence is configurable.

For I5 audience-binding tests on Casdoor as SP, the external IdP must be configured with SP Entity ID and ACS URL both set to https://<casdoor-domain>/api/acs. Wrong or missing audience/entity configuration at the IdP will cause login failure unrelated to the tested assertion audience semantics.

For I3 config-change tests involving SAML providers or applications, Casdoor docs only describe UI/Swagger-managed provider/application configuration and immediate use on subsequent logins. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of new logins before and after the same provider/application change; do NOT interpret a changed outcome after an admin reconfiguration as a bug by itself.

Application owner/tenant semantics matter in Casdoor. Users belong to an organization (owner = organization), while built-in/global admin resources are often managed under built-in/admin context. For multi-tenant SAML setup tests, the fuzzer MUST keep application/provider ownership consistent with the target organization or setup may silently fail for tenancy reasons unrelated to SAML security.

Numeric sentinel: application Code resend timeout uses 0 as a sentinel meaning 'use the global default', not literal zero seconds. Never assume 0 disables waiting; 0 selects the platform default countdown (default global value documented as 60 seconds).

Numeric sentinel: application CookieExpireInHours uses 0 as a sentinel meaning 'use default' rather than immediate expiry. Default is 720 hours, and without Remember Me the session is limited to 24 hours. Never use 0 expecting an instantly expired session.

Numeric sentinel: application RefreshExpireInHours defaults to 0 hours in docs for refresh token expiration configuration. Treat 0 as a special configuration value controlled by application settings, not as a generic 'expired immediately' assumption in tests.

For I2 freshness tests on SAML-backed OAuth sessions, include a control login using a valid flow before testing attack variants. A failed SAML login or token exchange can result from provider/application misconfiguration, missing provider attachment, or redirect mismatch rather than freshness enforcement.

Casdoor's /api/userinfo returns claims according to granted scope. For I4/I5 verification, the fuzzer MUST request the needed scopes during authorization/token exchange; otherwise missing email/profile fields in verify_granted_identity are by design and not evidence of identity loss or authorization stripping.

For RFC 8707 resource-indicator tests, the resource parameter must match exactly between /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token. If they differ, audience-related failures are expected setup failures, not I5 violations.

For token exchange scope-escalation tests, Casdoor documents that omitting scope inherits the subject token scope, while specifying scope is intended for narrowing. The fuzzer MUST compare requested scope against original scope and treat broader requested scopes as the attack case; inherited same-scope behavior is by design.

Casdoor supports subject_token_type values access_token, jwt, and id_token for token exchange. I5 token-exchange tests MUST set subject_token_type explicitly to match the actual token being exchanged; otherwise rejection may be due to token-type mismatch rather than audience/scope enforcement.
Casdoor's SAML ACS endpoint is /api/acs and accepts POST only. The fuzzer MUST use HTTP POST binding for saml_login; GET submissions are rejected by design.

saml.constraint: For SAML provider setup, Casdoor's SP Entity ID and ACS URL are the same value: https://<your-casdoor-domain>/api/acs. The external IdP MUST be configured with both fields set exactly to this URL or SAML setup is invalid.

Casdoor SAML login is IdP-initiated from the login page button and does not auto-redirect even when a single SAML provider is configured. Tests MUST explicitly initiate the SAML flow before posting the forged SAMLResponse; treating SAML as an automatic redirect flow will misconfigure the sequence.

Casdoor username mapping for SAML has fallback semantics: if the IdP does not explicitly provide a username mapping or the username field is empty, Casdoor first uses email as username, then falls back to NameID. I4 collision tests MUST account for this precedence; a missing username attribute may bind by email instead of NameID.

For I4 saml_email_binding_collision and cross-protocol merge tests, Casdoor may identify SAML users by email when username mapping is absent or empty. The fuzzer MUST control whether email is present and whether username mapping exists; otherwise identity merges by email are by design and can look like collisions.

Casdoor supports both GET and POST SAMLResponse only when acting as SAML IdP, depending on whether Reply URL is set. This does NOT apply to Casdoor as SP: /api/acs accepts POST only. SAML SP tests against Casdoor MUST not infer GET support from IdP-mode documentation.

Casdoor documents assertion signature compatibility control only for Casdoor acting as SAML IdP (Enable SAML assertion signature). This setting is not evidence about how Casdoor validates inbound SAML assertions as SP. The fuzzer MUST test inbound signature validation empirically via /api/acs and MUST NOT assume assertion-level signature requirements from IdP-mode docs.

For I1 SAML issuer validation tests, the external IdP metadata populates Endpoint, IdP, and Issuer URL in the Casdoor SAML provider. The fuzzer MUST configure a provider with parsed metadata first; otherwise issuer mismatch results may reflect missing provider trust configuration rather than issuer-validation behavior.

For I3 saml_mfa_bypass_via_binding_rule tests, Casdoor supports MFA on user accounts, but the provided docs do not expose a documented REST API endpoint to enable MFA programmatically. The fuzzer SHOULD treat MFA setup as unsupported-by-docs for automated setup in this profile to avoid false failures from missing admin APIs.

Application and provider ownership are tenant-scoped in Casdoor. Users belong to an organization, while applications/providers are created under an owner organization/admin context. For multi-tenant SAML tests, the fuzzer MUST keep organization ownership consistent across created users, applications, and providers or setup will not reflect the intended trust boundary.

Application tag restrictions are an authorization gate independent of SAML assertion contents. If application tags are configured, only users with at least one matching user tag may sign in, while admins are exempt. I5 SAML authorization tests MUST avoid unintended tag restrictions or they will produce false denials unrelated to SAML audience/attribute validation.

Exclusive sign-in is a by-design session policy: a new sign-in removes prior sessions for the same user and application. I2/I3 multi-login sequences MUST disable or account for EnableExclusiveSignin, or a second login invalidating the first session is not a replay/coherence bug.

Cookie/session lifetime has sentinel semantics: CookieExpireInHours default is 720 hours, but without Remember me the session is limited to 24 hours; value 0 means use default. Never assume 0 means immediate expiry. Freshness tests relying on session duration MUST account for this sentinel behavior.

Verification code resend timeout has sentinel semantics: application Code resend timeout value 0 means use the global default, not zero seconds. Never assume 0 disables waiting. This matters when password/MFA control logins are part of SAML bypass test setup.

Refresh token expiration has sentinel semantics: application RefreshExpireInHours defaults to 0 hours. The docs do not define 0 as immediate expiry in token responses; treat it as platform-configured behavior rather than literal zero-lifetime. Do not build freshness assertions on refresh-token expiry without a control test.

For I2 SAML replay tests, include a control login with a fresh, unique assertion before replaying the same assertion ID or OneTimeUse assertion. Without a successful control, a failed replay attempt cannot distinguish proper replay defense from broken SAML provider setup.

Casdoor's /api/userinfo returns claims according to the token scope and may include only sub/iss/aud for openid. Verification steps that compare granted identity or attributes after SAML login MUST request sufficient OAuth scopes during the surrounding authorization flow, or missing fields are by design.

Token introspection is protected by Basic Authentication using client_id:client_secret, not the bearer token itself. The fuzzer MUST supply client credentials when using introspect_token; a 401 without Basic auth is expected and not evidence of token invalidity.
